title: Ask why the wrong choice is wrong
statement: On a wrong choice, ask the learner why that option is not right before revealing the answer, so a retry becomes a thinking move instead of another guess.
example: In one design the move takes 0:25 and fires only on a wrong answer.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design adds a diagnose-the-distractor task to its task bank from Unit 2: on a wrong answer, ask why that one was not right before revealing (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 229-234). It rehearses no test item but turns the retry ladder into a thinking move, takes 0:25 and fires only on a wrong answer. The design's guardrails table proposes the same move for a child who collects the wrong evidence, as a match for tracking mistakes rather than grading (lines 74-77).
against: In the guardrails table the move is still a proposal (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 77).
